question: Japanese adults were trained to hear English r and l. Which training carried over best to voices they had never heard?
answer: Many different speakers. In studies from 1991 on, learners trained on five talkers improved and kept the gain with new voices; learners trained on one talker mostly learned that one voice. Variety taught them which differences mark the sound and which are just one person's way of speaking.
move: Learn from many examples, or you only learn the example.
ask: Am I learning a skill from one person's habits, or from enough variety to see the pattern?
trap: One clear speaker, because a clean model seems easier to copy.
reference: Logan, Lively & Pisoni, Training Japanese listeners to identify English /r/ and /l/: a first report, Journal of the Acoustical Society of America 89(2), 1991
